title: The three young men (Daniel 3)
hook: in the furnace they sing all ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, a song the Church prays on Sundays
carry: all ye works, bless the lord

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sirach, and one faithful friend. Your line was a friend is treasure. A new week starts.

King Nabuchodonosor of Babylon sets up a golden statue, sixty cubits high, on a plain. The order goes out: when you hear the music, the trumpet, the flute, the harp and all the rest, fall down and worship the statue, or be thrown into a burning furnace. The band strikes up, and the whole empire goes down on its face. Except three young Jews in the king's service: Ananias, Azarias and Misael, given the Babylonian names Sidrach, Misach and Abdenago. They stay standing. The king, furious, gives them one more chance: what god could deliver you out of my hand?
screen: `A GOLDEN STATUE, AND A BAND.` → `THREE YOUNG MEN STAY STANDING.` → `WHAT GOD COULD DELIVER YOU?`

segments.voice: Their answer doesn't bargain. Our God is able to save us from the furnace. But if he will not, know this, O king: we will not worship your gods. Even if not. The king has the furnace heated seven times hotter, so hot that the men who throw them in are killed by the flames. And the three walk around in the middle of the fire. In the Greek text of Daniel, which the Catholic Church receives as scripture, a long passage comes at this point: a prayer of Azarias in the fire, and then a song. Bibles that follow the Hebrew and Aramaic text, as Protestant Bibles do, leave it out or print it separately among the Apocrypha. The angel of the Lord comes down into the furnace, the text says, drives the flame out, and makes the middle of it like a cool, wet wind. And the three begin to sing. In Latin it's the Benedicite, from its first word: bless. In the Douay-Rheims: "All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever." Then the song calls on everything by name. Angels. Sun and moon. Stars. Showers and dew. Fire and heat. Cold and frost. Nights and days. Light and darkness. Mountains, seas, whales, birds, beasts. From inside a furnace, they tell fire and heat to bless the Lord. The Church still prays this canticle at Morning Prayer on Sundays and feasts.
screen: `BUT IF HE WILL NOT.` · `SEVEN TIMES HOTTER.` · `A SONG IN THE GREEK DANIEL.` · `FIRE AND HEAT, BLESS THE LORD.` · then, large: `ALL YE WORKS OF THE LORD, BLESS THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Let your eyes land on one thing that is simply there, the light, a tree, rain, the cup in your hand, your own breathing, and name it. The song does exactly this, calling each thing to praise God just by being what it is. If you pray, borrow its pattern: sun and moon, bless the Lord; nights and days, bless the Lord; if you don't, just be glad this one thing exists.
Benedicite. Latin for bless, the first word of the song of the three young men in the furnace, calling every creature to bless the Lord. Today's word.
Your line: all ye works, bless the lord. Even fire and heat. Day four hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: The canticle of the three young men from Daniel 3 is prayed at Morning Prayer of the Liturgy of the Hours on Sundays and feasts, and it is a traditional prayer of thanksgiving for priests after Mass.

original.note: Latin: bless ye (a command to many), the first word of the canticle; the Greek has eulogeite.

trapdoor: what you thought: three men who survived a fire.
what it means: three young men who refuse to bow even if God doesn't rescue them, and who sing a song calling all creation to bless God from inside the furnace.
what a scholar hears: the prayer of Azarias and the song of the three (Daniel 3:24–90 in the Douay) survive in Greek, not in the Hebrew-Aramaic text; Catholics and Orthodox read them as scripture.

chat.says: What did the three young men do inside the furnace?
options: They sang, calling every creature, even fire and heat, to bless the Lord.
They begged the king for mercy until he finally opened the furnace.
They stayed silent and waited, sure an angel would rescue them.
chat.meaning: In the Greek Daniel, which Catholics receive as scripture, the three sing the Benedicite, calling everything by name, fire and heat too, to bless the Lord.

Nabuchodonosor.meaning: the Douay's name for Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon

Azarias.meaning: one of the three young men; he prays in the fire

Apocrypha.meaning: books some Bibles print separately, not counted as scripture

canticle.meaning: a song from scripture, prayed in the liturgy
